newsitem.title: USA: Italy budget commitment sufficient for EMU-Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italy budget commitment sufficient for EMU-Ciampi.

text.p: Italy's 1997 budget bill is sufficient to get Italy into the European single currency, Treasury and Budget Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Sunday, standing by the budget's call for just over 62 trillion lire deficit cut.
"The figures are the ones I have given out. The committment (set in the budget bill) is sufficient" Ciampi told reporters after the IMF iInterim Committee meeting.
Reporters had queried Ciampi on a statement made Saturday in Italy by prime minister Romano Prodi.
Prodi had said that perhaps a further budget cut amounting to one percentage point of the GDP may have to be is needed to meet the three percent deficit/Gdp Maastricht criteria.

But the 1997 budget containment effort will enable Italy to negotiate on an equal level with its European partners, "because the effort is enourmous and they (the European partners) must recognise this," Prodi had said.
In his speech Saturday morning to the Interim Committee, Ciampi specified that the new budget Law "sets a new target: to reach a deficit to GDP ratio of 3 pct at the end of 1997".
The budget draft approved Friday by government includes a 12 trillion lire one-time tax levy which has been criticized for its possible one-off effects.
"This temporary tax will not slow down the path of budget consolidation, which will continue in 1998 in line with the targets of the three-year plan, Ciampi said in his speech.
